items.claim: The preview ghost painted hidden children of a dragged container, and children on hidden layers
The departure ghost painted a removed node that is `hidden`, and its subtree
The preview and departure ghosts ignored the scene slot's `drawnPose`, so they painted off the quantize grid
The worker decided whether the page builds the scene, and read `cull`, from the raw `layers.scene` prop instead of the slot resolved with presets
When `viewport.zoom`/`pan`/`touchZoom` re-registered, it buried a merged `actions` override
The `actions` prop missed actions owned by tools and contributions, because they register after the resolver runs
items.note: Only the partial-merge half of this was real. The resolver now re-applies on registry changes, and its "no default" warning waits until the commit's effects have run, so it no longer fires for an action registered later in the same commit. Not a defect: the claim that `actions={null}` should also mute tool and preset actions. `SceneCanvas.actions.test.tsx` asserts on purpose that null spares them ("opts out of the kit's defaults, not out of the presets you passed").

items.claim: Content bounds were cached on `getVersion()`, which pose overrides and scroll offsets don't bump
`colorAt` ignored `layerOrder`, so it sampled layers left out of the paint and stacked them in the wrong order
Hover was only tracked when the `chromeVisibility` prop or `onHover` was given
`useBakedScene` returned a later `SerializedScene` prop cast as a live `Scene`, which threw on first use
items.note: I made a strict call here and recorded it in `docs/unruled.md`: the canvas keeps the last live scene and warns once.
